newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbian factions cautiously back election ruling.
newsitem.headline: Serbian factions cautiously back election ruling.

text.p: Rival Serbian factions gave a cautious welcome to decisions on Tuesday restoring victories in annulled municipal elections to opponents of President Slobodan Milosevic.

The opposition Zajedno (Together) coalition applauded rulings awarding them victories in Serbia's two biggest cities, Belgrade and Nis, but vowed to continue protests until all their wins in 14 of Serbia's 18 biggest cities are verified.
Moderates and member parties of the ruling Socialist coalition meanwhile urged their backers not to become upset because, they said, the rule of law was being respected.

"Because of our bad experiences with the Socialists, we do not trust them and will continue demonstrating until the verification of the very last mandate in the city council of Belgrade, but also in all other towns in Serbia," said Slobodan Vuksanovic, spokesman for the opposition Democratic Party.
Zajedno and students have been demonstrating for two months to force the government to overturn its annulment of opposition electoral victories on November 17.
The opposition won a major breakthrough when electoral officials in the capital Belgrade overruled a district court to award victory to Zajedno in the city assembly.
Independent media said a court in Serbia's second largest city Nis made a similar ruling there.

The rulings came after as many as half a million people massed in Belgrade for an Orthodox New Year's Eve rally that was the biggest demonstration to date against the autocratic Milosevic's government.
Dusan Mihajlovic, a leader of the moderate New Democracy party allied with the Socialists, said the ruling in Belgrade showed the law was being applied.
"I think it is a good decision and that it's particularly good because it was taken within the framework of the legal possibilities which are at our disposal," he said.
"The Socialists can file a complaint to the electoral commission...But I think that using these legal means would not be politically wise and correct..."
Even the Yugoslav United Left (JUL), headed by Milosevic's wife, endorsed the decision and urged its backers to accept the Belgrade electoral commission's action.
"The decision taken by the municipal electoral commission and announced today is not anything that should either amaze, elate, frighten or encourage anyone," JUL spokesman Alexsandar Vulin said.
"It is simply a decision reached not on the basis of any political deals but simply one founded on the law, the constitution and insight into the electoral process which took place on November 17."
The official Tanjug news agency suggested more legal manoeuvring lay ahead.
"Legal experts told Tanjug that they could give their precise assessment of the commission's decision only after reading it carefully," the report said.
